Q1: Sethoxydim exhibits known acute and chronic environmental hazards based on GHS classification (Tier 1). While oral hazards and endocrine disruption potential are characterized as low to moderate (Tier 3), significant data gaps exist for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive hazards, inhalation, dermal/eye, and organ/systemic hazards (Tier 4).
